# Archive: TEST-SCRIPT-REVIEW.md

# Test Script and Protocol Review

**Reviewed:** 2026-10-06  
**Scope:** the Vitest and Playwright suites, their support modules, runner
configuration, package scripts, test-governance guards, measurement scripts,
and the repository instructions that tell contributors which command to run.

## Executive finding

The individual product tests are generally unusually strong: the suite has
direct exported-artifact checks, fault-injection history, real-click coverage,
classified skips, and guards against vacuous Excel/PDF round trips. The main
risk is now the test infrastructure around those tests. Several named tiers do
not guarantee the target they claim, parts of the governance are enforced by
shallow text scans, one browser test can pass without testing anything, and a
branch-only Milestone 70 guard is still presented as live tooling even though
it cannot pass on the current branch.

No defect found here changes a filed value by itself. The effect is indirect
but important: a contributor can receive a green result from a different
browser/target, omit a release-only test, or retain a vacuous test while
believing the promised regression was run.

### Priority summary

| ID | Priority | Finding | Practical consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | High | `npm test` and `test:quick` inherit `PG_TARGET` / `PG_BROWSER` | A command documented as source/Chromium can silently test another target or browser. |
| T2 | High | Local Playwright reuses any server already answering the configured port | A green run can exercise another checkout or an old process rather than this worktree. |
| T3 | High | One E2E test is vacuous when its subject disappears | Removing or hiding Save Backup lets the “save event fires” test pass with no assertion. |
| T4 | High | No repository-defined automation enforces the named gates | A commit can land without quick, verify, or release validation; README's CI claim is unsupported here. |
| T5 | Medium | Release-profile membership is hand-maintained and unguarded | A target-only test can be skipped by source and omitted from the only profile that could run it. |
| T6 | Medium | Skip classification is syntactic, incomplete, and already semantically misused | New skips can evade the audit; nine obsolete merge-comparison cases are counted as expected target exclusions. |
| T7 | Medium | `TEST-INDEX.md` governance does not cover the runner's full discovery rules or its own selection matrix | A nested/TypeScript unit spec can be unindexed, while a lite-test instruction already names a deleted test. |
| T8 | Medium | The Milestone 70 ledger guard is retired in practice but live in the tree | Running the advertised guard on `master` fails on 128 legitimate commits; its unit spec does not exercise that failure. |
| T9 | Low | The assertion-count tripwire records test counts but never compares them | A test declaration can disappear without a recorded reason if the file's static `expect()` count does not fall. |
| T10 | Low | Fixed sleeps remain in 17 E2E files | Positive-state tests can be slower or flaky on this FAT32 workstation; some negative observation windows are justified. |
| T11 | Low | Test instructions and target vocabulary have drifted | Contributors are told there are four targets/six profiles and to run an unauthorized full suite before every commit. |

## Review snapshot and method

This was a read-only audit of test behavior plus this report. Per `AGENTS.md`,
the full regression was not run without explicit approval. Discovery was
compiled without executing tests:

- Vitest listed 2,690 test cases in 182 unit spec files in the current
  worktree.
- Playwright listed 1,069 source/Chromium cases. It reported 154 source files;
  the filesystem has 153 `*.spec.ts` files because some generated tests are
  attributed to an imported support module.
- `test:quick` lists 69 browser cases in four files.
- The curated profiles list 36 web cases, 32 `file://` portable cases, 33
  portable-over-HTTP cases, and 119 cases per cross-browser smoke run.
- Static scans found no committed `.only` or `.fixme`, and no direct
  `test.skip()` call in an E2E spec. There are 14 classified skip call sites
  and 28 `waitForTimeout()` calls across 17 E2E files.
- The two untracked specs in the concurrent worktree
  (`stamped-co-guardian.spec.ts` and `started-guardian.spec.js`) were read but
  not reported as index/baseline defects; they are visibly part of unfinished
  Milestone 73/74 work.

The audit covered every discovered spec through inventory and static scans,
then read the runner/configuration code and each flagged call site. It did not
claim that a list-only compile proves runtime behavior.

## Detailed findings

### T1 — The named default tiers do not pin source/Chromium (High)

What a maintainer sees: `npm test` is documented as “the complete source E2E
suite / source / chromium,” but it can run against `web`, `portable`, Firefox,
WebKit, or Edge if those variables remain in the shell from an earlier manual
command. `test:quick` has the same problem. With `PG_TARGET=web`, it can also
test an old `dist/web` because the quick tier does not build first.

Evidence:

- `package.json:13` defines `test:e2e` as bare `playwright test`.
- `package.json:23-24` compose both named tiers from bare Playwright.
- `playwright.config.ts:12-13` accepts `PG_TARGET` and `PG_BROWSER` from the
  caller and falls back only when each is absent.
- `package.json:14` already has a runner that pins source/Chromium, but
  `npm test` does not use it.

Recommendation: make named tiers set their own target and browser in a
cross-platform wrapper. Preserve bare `npx playwright test` as the documented
expert escape hatch. Because `AGENTS.md` explicitly freezes the meaning of
`npm test`, treat this as a named workflow decision: the observable meaning
stays “full source/Chromium,” while deliberate custom runs remain direct
Playwright commands.

Acceptance check: start a shell with `PG_TARGET=portable` and
`PG_BROWSER=firefox`; the list output from `npm test -- --list` and the browser
half of `test:quick` must still identify source/Chromium.

### T2 — A local run can attach to the wrong server (High)

What a maintainer sees: if any process is already answering on port 4321,
4173, 5173, or 4341, Playwright may reuse it. It verifies that the URL answers,
not that the process serves this checkout or commit. A green run can therefore
describe an old build or another copy of the repository.

Evidence: `playwright.config.ts:89` sets `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`.
The measurement scripts already recognize this failure mode and explicitly
refuse busy ports; the main E2E runner does not.

Recommendation: default to `reuseExistingServer: false` for verification
commands. If fast interactive reuse is worth keeping, put it behind an
explicit opt-in and verify a per-run build/checkout marker before accepting
the server.

Acceptance check: serve a different page on 4321, then start the source test
tier. It must stop with a clear port-ownership error rather than list/run tests
against that page.

### T3 — The backup-event test passes when Save Backup is gone (High)

What a maintainer sees: the test named “deterministic save event hook fires
with the expected filename” succeeds if the sidebar Save Backup button is
missing or hidden—the exact regression that makes the behavior unavailable to
a filer.

Evidence: `tests/e2e/verified-inventory-workflow.spec.ts:98-119` puts the
listener, click, and both assertions inside
`if (await saveBtn.isVisible())`. There is no `else` failure and no assertion
before the condition.

Recommendation: require the button with `await expect(saveBtn).toBeVisible()`,
then install the listener and click it. If the original concern is a dangling
listener during teardown, visibility should be proven before creating the
promise, not used to skip the test body.

Required verification for a future fix: red-first by temporarily removing or
hiding the action and confirming this specific test fails because the Save
Backup control is unavailable.

### T4 — The repository has named gates but no repository-defined gate runner (High)

What a maintainer sees: `test:quick`, `test:verify`, and `test:release` are
commands, not enforced gates. Nothing in the repository runs one on a push or
prevents a merge when it is omitted.

Evidence:

- There is no `.github/`, `.husky/`, GitLab, or Azure pipeline configuration,
  and `core.hooksPath` is unset.

  > **Correction (2026-10-12 recheck, added by Claude at the requester's
  > request):** the repository root is `D:\caernarvon-net`, one level above
  > `probate-guardian/`, and it has `.github/workflows/probate-guardian-tests.yml`.
  > It ran on every push and pull request touching `probate-guardian/**` until
  > `5dfe35c` (2026-09-13) and has run only on manual dispatch since, with a
  > 15-minute limit the full source suite cannot meet. The finding's substance
  > stands: nothing enforces a gate, and README's CI claim is untrue in
  > practice. See `TEST-REVIEW.md` section 2.2.
- `README.md:65-66` nevertheless says CI runs the source suite and a release
  matrix.
- `package.json:26` defines the release command, but no repository automation
  invokes it.

This does not prove an external CI service does not exist. It does mean a
fresh clone contains no way to reproduce or inspect the claimed automation.

Recommendation: either add a repository-visible pipeline or rewrite the claim
as an external/manual obligation and record where its results live. A
proportionate first gate is type/data-model/unit plus the quick browser tier on
ordinary changes, with the expensive release matrix manual, scheduled, or
release-triggered. Enabling automatic full/release execution is a requester
decision because current policy requires approval for full regressions.

### T5 — Curated release profiles can silently omit the tests that need them (Medium)

What a maintainer sees: the release command sounds comprehensive, but only the
source/Chromium leg is the whole browser suite. The built and cross-browser
legs are manually curated arrays. Adding a web-only regression test does not
put it in the web profile; if the test skips under source, the release run can
execute it nowhere.

Evidence:

- `scripts/run-e2e-profile.mjs:30-60` hard-codes three lists.
- The current lists discover 36 web, 32 portable, 33 portable-HTTP, and 119
  cross-browser cases versus 1,069 source cases.
- `scripts/run-e2e-profile.mjs:65-76` is the only membership mapping.
- The skip audit checks spelling/classification, not whether every
  target-dependent test is selected by a runnable profile.

The reduced matrices are intentional and should remain reduced. The defect is
that no machine-checkable ownership connects a distribution-sensitive test to
the profile that exercises it.

Recommendation: tag or declare profile membership beside each test/spec and
derive the lists, or add a unit guard that parses all target-sensitive specs
and proves at least one release profile runs each non-source branch. Also add
a guard that every configured target and browser appears in the shared
vocabulary exactly once.

### T6 — Skip governance is easy to bypass, and the merge gate is misclassified (Medium)

What a maintainer sees: a test can be disabled without the audit noticing by
using `test .skip`, `test.fixme`, `test.describe.skip`, an alias, or a nested
spec directory. Even a correctly detected helper call is not checked for the
right category.

Evidence:

- `tests/unit/skip-classification-audit.spec.js:51-58` scans only top-level
  `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` and looks only for the exact regex
  `\btest\.skip\(`.
- Playwright discovery is recursive, and its API has more disable forms than
  the regex recognizes.
- `tests/e2e/pre-merge-output.characterization.spec.ts:56` classifies absence
  of `PG_PREMERGE_SHA` as an `expected-target-exclusion`. It is not a target
  capability; it is a retired/on-demand merge workflow.
- That file contributes nine skipped cases to ordinary discovery and every
  default release run.
- `tests/e2e/support/target-profile.ts:65` still points readers to the deleted
  `skip-classification-audit.spec.ts` instead of the unit spec that replaced
  it.

Recommendation: replace the skip regex with an AST-based audit that walks the
same recursive file set as Playwright and recognizes all disable forms and
aliases. Move the pre-merge comparison to a dedicated command/config outside
ordinary discovery, or give it an explicit workflow-gated category and runner.
If `skipTemporaryGap` remains, enforce its documented milestone-file check;
the helper currently accepts any string.

### T7 — The test-index guard does not guard the whole index (Medium)

What a maintainer sees: `TEST-INDEX.md` can tell someone to run a file that no
longer exists, while the index guard stays green. It can also miss a unit
TypeScript spec or any nested spec even though the runner executes it.

Evidence:

- Vitest discovers `tests/unit/**/*.spec.{js,ts}`
  (`vitest.config.ts:10`), but
  `tests/unit/test-index-guard.spec.js:13` scans only top-level `*.spec.js`.
- The E2E half at line 14 is also top-level only.
- The guard validates only the first cell of primary file rows; it does not
  validate the category/scope selection tables used for lite testing.
- `TEST-INDEX.md:454` still directs `pdf-export / all forms` changes to
  `attestation-layout.spec.ts`, deleted when its coverage moved into
  `schedule-card-layout.spec.ts` (`TEST-INDEX.md:331`).
- Basename-only comparison would also conflate a unit and E2E spec if they
  ever shared a filename.

Recommendation: compare repository-relative paths recursively, using the
actual Vitest and Playwright globs. Parse and validate every spec token in the
category/scope tables separately from historical prose. Add a synthetic
fault test for nested specs, unit `.spec.ts`, duplicate basenames, and stale
matrix references.

### T8 — The Milestone 70 ledger guard is obsolete and misleading (Medium)

What a maintainer sees: running the advertised ledger guard on the current
`master` reports the repository itself as invalid.

Evidence:

- `scripts/ms70-ledger-guard.mjs:4-14` describes a temporary branch workflow
  that ended when Milestone 70 merged.
- Its default upstream remains `origin/master` (`:95`).
- On 2026-10-06, `node scripts/ms70-ledger-guard.mjs --no-fetch` exited 1:
  140 commits since the branch point, 128 “unlisted,” including the Milestone
  70 merge and all later milestones.
- `tests/unit/ms70-ledger-guard.spec.js:72-81` checks only that the historical
  branch point is present and the table parses. It never runs the real current
  guard or proves it is usable.

Recommendation: remove the script, its unit spec, and their active file-index
claims, while retaining the ledger itself as historical evidence. If the
parser is worth preserving, move it to an archive/tool test that does not
claim to be a current gate. This deletion requires the normal `TEST-INDEX.md`
and `file_index.md` updates.

Related cleanup: `ms70-declaration-dispositions.spec.js` now asserts an empty
declaration list after the monolith's deletion while
`ms70-monolith-deleted.spec.js`, `window-bridge.spec.js`, and the dependency
ratchet protect the live invariant. Review it for archival retirement, but do
not remove the dependency/state/window ratchets merely because their names
still say `ms70`; those continue to inspect current source and catch real
architecture regressions.

### T9 — Assertion-count governance ignores its own test count (Low)

What a maintainer sees: the baseline records both assertion calls and test
declarations, but only fewer assertions fail the comparison. Removing a test
declaration while leaving helper assertions in the file needs no recorded
reason.

Evidence:

- `scripts/ms70-assertion-counts.mjs:54-56` counts tests.
- `compareCounts()` at `:88-95` compares only `now.expects` with
  `was.expects`.
- `tests/unit/ms70-assertion-counts.spec.js:53-56` trusts that incomplete
  comparison.

The script correctly calls itself a tripwire rather than semantic proof; it
should not be deleted. Recommendation: compare both counts and log each kind
of drop. Add a synthetic case where a test declaration falls but the expect
count does not. Continue requiring fault injection/red-first proof for
meaningful regressions, because counts can never establish assertion quality.

### T10 — Fixed sleeps should be narrowed, not blanket-replaced (Low)

The suite has 28 `waitForTimeout()` calls across 17 files. Several are valid
negative observation windows or protocol clocks: “no reload,” an autosave
debounce, two lock heartbeats, and the historical auto-tour timer. The PDF.js
annotation tests also record why no usable readiness signal exists.

The weaker positive-state sleeps are in files such as
`sidebar-total-follows-changes.spec.ts`, `guardian-links-follow-rows.spec.ts`,
and `signature-by-hand.spec.ts`; they wait 200–500 ms and then inspect state.
On the FAT32 test drive, fixed durations are more likely to create intermittent
failures than an assertion-driven `expect.poll()` or locator wait.

Recommendation: replace waits that precede a positive observable state with
polling for that state. Keep deliberate absence windows, but name the product
timer/heartbeat they exceed and assert the forbidden event did not occur.

### T11 — Maintainer instructions have drifted from the runnable suite (Low)

Evidence:

- `README.md:64-66` says four targets and claims a CI matrix. The suite now has
  `portable-http`, and no repository CI definition exists.
- `HOW-TO-RUN.txt:63` says `all-profiles` runs six profiles. It runs seven,
  including `portable-http`; that profile's direct command is absent from the
  surrounding list.
- `TEST-INDEX.md:468-500` says full `npm test` is required before every commit.
  `AGENTS.md` now says lite by default and requires the requester's explicit
  go-ahead before any full regression.
- `tests/e2e/support/target-profile.ts:3-4` calls itself the single source of
  truth from which `playwright.config.ts` derives, but the config and profile
  runner each carry independent hard-coded target maps.

Recommendation: after the runner decisions above, update the three documents
from one authoritative profile manifest. Keep dated performance numbers dated;
do not turn list counts into undated promises.

## Protocols that remain effective

These should be retained while the items above are repaired:

- `vitest.config.ts` explicitly excludes E2E files and fails on zero unit-test
  discovery.
- Playwright is serialized intentionally (`workers: 1`) and records failure
  traces locally and on CI retry.
- Export tests commonly inspect the produced PDF/XLSX directly rather than
  trusting the app's importer. This is the correct protection for court
  output.
- The current dependency, state-authority, window-bridge, data-model, and
  formula/defined-name guards inspect live source or output and remain useful
  despite milestone-prefixed filenames.
- The source Chromium leg of `test:release` is full and is not duplicated;
  web/portable builds occur within their own profile steps.
- No focused or disabled `.only`/`.fixme` was found.

## Recommended remediation order

1. Make the vacuous Save Backup test fail when its control is missing (T3).
2. Pin named tiers and stop wrong-server reuse (T1, T2).
3. Repair the index and instruction drift (T7, T11).
4. Retire the ledger guard and separate the on-demand pre-merge comparison
   from ordinary discovery (T6, T8).
5. Add machine-checked profile ownership and repository-visible automation
   after the requester chooses the cost/frequency (T4, T5).
6. Harden the assertion and wait tripwires as maintenance work (T9, T10).

The runner/profile and automation items are decision-driven because they
change what contributors observe and how much validation runs automatically.
This report identifies them; it does not silently choose that cost.

# Archive: TEST-REVIEW.md

# Test Protocol Remediation Plan

**Prepared:** 2026-10-06

**Last amended:** 2026-10-13 (recheck of 2026-10-12, section 2.2; run time
made a completion requirement, section 2.3 and Delivery 1M; Delivery 1 built)

**Status:** Approved for implementation 2026-10-13 by the requester ("Implement
TEST-REVIEW.md": all deliveries in order, including 6 and 7; the decisions the plan
reserves for the requester -- 1M's target and consolidations, 4P's go/no-go,
Delivery 5's manual run -- stay theirs). **Built: Delivery 1 (2026-10-13,
`4f6b864`); Delivery 1M (2026-10-14, `2938f4f`, `dce9dfa`, `39384bc`, `db8e1f5e`; `npm test` on C:
43.1 min, was 110); Delivery 2 (2026-10-14, `cc66ae4`); Delivery 3 (2026-10-14, `ed53d32a`); Delivery 4 (2026-10-14, `b19d8392`, after the 4P prototype); Delivery 5 (2026-10-15, `fb20e4ea`, `7c90b1bf`; the manual run's unit fixes `396e2a30`); Delivery 6 (2026-10-15, three measured items, `caca81b8`, `d3064f64`, `3be3bbc8`); Delivery 7 (2026-10-15, `cc328fa6`).**

**Scope:** Bounded repairs to execution and test governance, and a measured cut
in run time. Modularization, coverage expansion and selective archiving are
separately approved follow-ups.

## 1. Purpose And Revised Direction

A filer must be able to enter information, preserve it through saving and
reopening, and receive faithful court output. A maintainer must also know that
a green result exercised the intended checkout, build, browser, and behavior.
Neither assurance can substitute for the other. And a regression should cost
no more time than its evidence needs: the 2026-10-12 full run took 1 h 50 min
(section 2.3).

This updates the earlier domain-based outline in light of Codex's
[Test Script and Protocol Review](TEST-SCRIPT-REVIEW.md). Its findings concern
strong individual tests surrounded by unreliable execution and governance
promises. Codex's subsequent critique correctly identifies excessive scope in
the first draft, and the follow-up review correctly recommends implementation
evidence between deliveries rather than approval of the initial three as one
package. This revision separates protocol repair from broader ambitions:

1. Truthful execution: T3, T1, T2 and immediate T11 documentation corrections;
   then 1M, measured minimization: per-case setup cost, the heavy-spec parallel
   probe and a redundancy audit by proof role, then the reductions they justify
   (added 2026-10-13).
2. Executable governance: T6, T7, T8 and T9.
3. Domain-valid fixture contracts and fail-fast output preconditions: N1.
4. Target-case runtime prototype, then a minimal profile manifest if proven: T5.
5. Automation decision and separately authorized configuration: T4.
6. Optional modularization/coverage work, only for demonstrated problems.
7. Selective historical archiving, only for genuinely retired tools.

Deliveries 1, 1M and 2-4 define the initial remediation completion boundary,
including a measured cut in full-source run time (section 10; added 2026-10-13
at the requester's decision). Neither a
full-suite archive nor new product coverage is a prerequisite. T10 cleanup is
opportunistic when its tests are touched, not an acceptance gate. Integrate
verified instructions into [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) without implying that optional
follow-ups or automation are already approved.

Approve and implement these deliveries sequentially, not as a package:

1. Delivery 1 may be approved now, but only within its explicit narrow boundary.
   Delivery 1M follows it and is approved separately; its measurements set the
   runtime target.
2. Finalize and approve Delivery 2 after Delivery 1 supplies real runner and
   discovery evidence. Its parser recognizes documented ordinary forms and
   reports ambiguous forms for review; it is not a JavaScript data-flow analyzer.
3. Finalize and approve Delivery 3 separately after inspecting the actual
   positive fixture/export helpers and bounding the affected forms. Do not fold
   it into Delivery 1 or an MS74 product change implicitly.
4. Do not approve Delivery 4 until a separately authorized small prototype proves
   that one target-specific case is selected, runs rather than skips, and reaches
   its relevant assertion. Manifest membership alone is insufficient evidence.

Keep Vitest/Playwright, real-click tests, independent artifact inspections,
failure traces, zero-discovery failures, and useful live-source architecture
ratchets. Milestone-prefixed names alone are not grounds for retirement.
Writing this plan does not change product code, persisted data, calculations,
commands, archives, tests, or AGENTS rules.

## 2. Evidence And Scope

T1-T11 are the original remediation inputs, not a claim that this exercise reran Codex's
audit. Nearby inspection confirmed the conditional Save Backup assertions,
environment-sensitive Playwright configuration, server reuse, curated profile
arrays, top-level-only index/skip scans, assertion-only count comparison, and
contradictory lite-test instructions. Counts, timing, retired-ledger runtime
failure, and automation inventory remain dated audit evidence to recheck.
They were rechecked on 2026-10-12 (section 2.2); the automation inventory
was wrong.

N1 is additional evidence from the 2026-10-07 MS74 regression. A positive
workbook-placement fixture generated the arbitrary text `V0010` for `county`;
current validation correctly rejected it, while the export helper waited up to
three minutes for a download that could not begin. Repairing the fixture to use
a real Florida county exposed, but did not by itself resolve, a separate Preview
acknowledgement lifecycle defect. This plan treats fixture validity, fail-fast
helper diagnostics and incidental product defects as three distinct concerns.

Do not reset, stash, archive as settled, or retire another contributor's work.
When this plan was written the worktree held concurrent product, fixture,
baseline and index edits and was ahead of origin; it is now clean and level
with origin (2026-10-12 recheck, section 2.2). Select an agreed clean committed
reference only when preservation is scoped.

Tests prove implemented behavior and output fidelity, not legal sufficiency
or guaranteed clerk acceptance. Legal wording, calculations, thresholds, and
form differences require reviewed provenance. County practice must not become
a statewide requirement through a test.

### 2.3 Where The Run Time Goes, 2026-10-12

*Added 2026-10-13 by Claude at the requester's request, after Codex's
efficiency review. The requester's reasons for this refactor include cutting
the time a regression takes, and a measured cut is now a completion
requirement (section 10, Delivery 1M). Measured from the list-reporter log of
the 2026-10-12 full `npm test` on C: -- 1,222 executed browser cases, 101.9
minutes of test time in a run of 1 h 50 min that includes the unit tests --
and from Milestone 59's runtime record. Codex's figures below were each
confirmed.*

- **No single spec dominates.** The largest is `navigation-status.contract`
  (96 cases, 5.1 min, 5%). The ten slowest specs take 31% of the time, the
  thirty slowest 54%, across 182 files. By case count the largest are
  `navigation-status.contract` 96, `sav-corpus.characterization` 66,
  `signature-capture.contract` 36, `routes` 33,
  `excel-form-field-placement` 28 (5.0 min), `output-buttons-after-override`
  23 and `readiness-card.contract` 21. The slowest single cases are
  `asterisks-follow-rules`' Annual (78 s) and Inventory (57 s), which drive
  every page of a form.
- **Every case pays a floor.** Median 3.6 s, fastest tenth 2.6 s, slowest
  tenth 7.7 s or more; 77% of cases take 5 s or less. 1,222 cases x 2.6 s =
  53 min, about half the run. Most of it is presumably the setup nearly every
  case repeats (load the app, start a case, create a filing); that is
  unmeasured. Removing a case saves its 3-5 s; a cheaper setup saves on every
  case.
- **Parallel workers have unfollowed evidence.** Milestone 59's probe
  (`tests/baseline/milestone-59-runtime.json`, entry 59C-4): four light
  contract specs, 139 cases, went from 273 s serial to 139-140 s at four
  workers, three runs, no failures or flakes, and the config's claim that
  concurrent contexts overload the shared server did not reproduce. The heavy
  specs (PDF, Excel, downloads, service worker, cross-tab) were never probed;
  the record estimates that probe at about ten minutes. `workers: 1` remains
  (`playwright.config.ts:110`).
- **Release-only costs.** A release selects 1,699 browser cases: the 1,238
  source cases, web 36, portable 32, portable-http 33, and 120 on each of
  Firefox, WebKit and Edge. `navigation-status.contract` is 96 of each extra
  browser's 120 cases -- 288 extra executions -- and 5.1 of the 6.6
  Chromium-minutes that list takes. `all` builds the portable artifact twice
  (`scripts/run-e2e-profile.mjs:68`, `:73`); Vite reported 13 s for one such
  build on 2026-10-13. The release gate is optional and rarely run, so these
  savings do not touch the everyday full run.
- **Skips.** Portable selects 32 cases and skips 12 as expected target
  exclusions. A skipped case ends before its work, so this costs clarity more
  than time.
- **The drive.** Browser tests run about twice as slowly from D: (FAT32) as
  from a copy on C: (NTFS) (AGENTS.md section 1). Running full regressions
  from C: is already the practice, and the largest saving in use.

Do not implement T1's acceptance literally as `npm test -- --list`: forwarding
through a compound unit/browser script does not reliably isolate browser
discovery and may execute units. Inspect the wrapper's child invocation and use
direct, explicitly pinned Playwright discovery where useful; Delivery 1 adds no
runner list API. Server provenance requires a minimal runtime collision check.

### 3.1 Server Collision Diagnostics (T2)

An occupied port must fail verification with the profile, URL/port and a clear
explanation that the existing process was not reused. On Windows, suggest
`Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen` to find OwningProcess,
then `Get-Process -Id <pid>` to inspect it. Only after the maintainer confirms
ownership should they stop it with `Stop-Process -Id <pid>` or its original
terminal. Do not kill unknown listeners, demand elevation, or equate a Vite/Node
process name with proof that it is an orphan. If process details are unavailable,
report that limitation while retaining the actionable port diagnostic.

Use Playwright's ordinary owned-server lifecycle and verify cleanup after normal
success and child failure. Delivery 1 does not add signal forwarding, process-tree
killing, orphan reclamation or a custom interruption manager. A preflight check
can race a later bind, so startup collision errors must also remain explicit and
fatal. When that late failure is Playwright's own "already used" error, the
runner recognises it in the child's output and prints the same port-inspection
guidance after it; this reads output only and adds no process handling
(2026-10-13, after Antigravity's review). An orphaned server is a reason for diagnostic cleanup by its confirmed
owner, not permission for silent reuse.

Delivery 1 does not introduce interactive reuse or a build/head stamp. Owned
startup and a fresh build are the baseline. A future reuse proposal would need
a served per-run checkout/build identifier and handshake; a HEAD-only stamp
cannot distinguish dirty checkouts or stale builds. Scope that separately rather
than inventing a dynamic backend for static Vite verification.

## 4. Classification Vocabulary, Not Directory Reorganization

### 4.1 Domain Modules

| Module | Contracts And Sub-Tests |
| --- | --- |
| Filing data | Defaults, tri-state, normalization idempotence, field domains, form-specific factories, bounds and legacy migration without silent loss. |
| Identity/lifecycle | Party/case resolution, merge chains, unlink/re-index, create/open/switch/delete, archived years, permitted conversions and carry/reset rules. |
| Accounting/validation | Money/percentage/rounding boundaries, dates, requiredness, attorney absence, county applicability, readiness/advisory/override distinctions. |
| Form interaction | Input/draft/commit, formatting, add/remove/duplicate, hide without deletion, real navigation, error focus, mount/dispose and failed loads. |
| Persistence/recovery | Queue/flush, save/load/backup/import, encrypted/plain cases, corrupt/partial files, rollback, storage failure and interruption/recovery. |
| Security/privacy | Real crypto, wrong password/tampering, lock/unlock, hostile input/files, masking, plaintext/log/cache/network boundaries. |
| Court artifacts | Actual XLSX/PDF, imports, placement, formulas/names/merges/print areas, amounts, signatures, attachments, text and geometry. |
| Delivery/usability | Source/dev/hosted/portable/subfolder, offline/update, browsers, keyboard/screen reader, contrast/responsive layouts, performance/lifecycle growth. |
| Test infrastructure | Discovery, runner precedence, server/build identity, profile ownership, skips, indexes, counts, baseline review, archive exclusion and reports. |

Cover all nine filing identities: Guardian Inventory, Annual/Final/Trust
Accounting, Simplified Accounting, and Initial/Annual/Minor/Simplified Plans.
Shared engines do not erase distinct wording, capabilities, and carry rules.

### 4.2 Layers

1. **Unit:** exhaustive inexpensive rule and boundary checks without a browser.
2. **Integration/contract:** real relevant collaborators; mock outer effects,
   not the rule under test. Include failure and rollback contracts.
3. **Feature/UI:** real browser fields/cards/pages without full-case setup when unnecessary.
4. **Artifact:** generate and independently inspect outputs, not just re-import them.
5. **Journey:** selected complete workflows crossing module boundaries.
6. **Infrastructure:** synthetic faulty suites/configs plus minimal real runner checks.
7. **Manual/specialist:** accessibility, spreadsheet evaluation/rendering,
   print fidelity, reference review and exploratory usability.

Keep existing test directories and paths. These domains/layers are vocabulary
for optional tags and human selection, not authorization to move hundreds of
files. Move a spec only while materially revising it, with import, baseline,
index and historical-reference updates. Separating the workflow-only pre-merge
comparison is a targeted discovery repair, not a general reorganization.

### 4.3 Candidate Minimal Profile Manifest

The manifest is a candidate design, not yet an approved mechanism. Before its
full implementation is requested, run the separately authorized Delivery 4
prototype described below and revise or reject this design from that evidence.

Propose `tests/profile-manifest.json` (new, not implemented). Reuse
`scripts/run-e2e-profile.mjs` as the only browser execution wrapper. The
manifest contains explicit entries for curated-tier/profile members and
historical exceptions, not every ordinary unit or source E2E spec. Each entry
records only:

- Repository-relative spec path.
- Active or historical status.
- Tier membership.
- Applicable profile IDs from the executable registry, not repeated target/browser values.
- External prerequisite, if any. Build requirements stay in the registry and are referenced, not copied.
- Optional domain/filing tags for human selection.

Where a file mixes target-specific and ordinary cases, a curated profile
selects the cases it needs rather than the whole file -- by narrowly scoped
specs or by case metadata -- and a curated release profile contains no
expected-target-exclusion skips: a case that cannot run there is not selected
there (2026-10-13, after Codex's efficiency review). This is a clarity rule more than a time saving, since a
skipped case ends before its work (section 2.3).

Keep ownership deliberately non-overlapping:

- One executable profile registry owns profile IDs, target/browser values,
  build prerequisites and whether a profile belongs to the release sequence.
- The manifest owns curated spec membership and its status/tier/prerequisite/tag
  metadata. Once accepted, it replaces
  `HOSTED_PARITY_SPECS`, `PORTABLE_PARITY_SPECS`,
  `CROSS_BROWSER_SMOKE_SPECS` and the fixed quick list; those paths must not
  remain copied in the runner or package scripts.
- Playwright configuration owns server URLs/commands and browser launch details,
  keyed and exhaustively checked against the registry rather than declaring a
  separate valid-profile vocabulary.
- `target-profile.ts` owns test-visible target capabilities, keyed and checked
  against the same registry. It does not redefine runnable tier membership.

Do not put the same target/browser/build fields in both the registry and the
manifest. Repeated identifiers used as checked keys are acceptable; repeated
authoritative values or membership lists are not.

Do not add a manual source-dependency graph, contract/owner ledger, layer
inventory or duplicated schema. Changed-file suggestions remain advisory and
cannot suppress tests or certify coverage. Contributors still inspect shared
consumers and recommend broader checks under current AGENTS rules.

Use one shared target/browser/profile vocabulary consumed by the runner,
Playwright configuration and target helpers. The manifest describes curated
membership; full source still discovers all active product specs using the
actual runner rules, not a manifest allowlist. Audit missing/stale/duplicate
paths and membership instead of letting missing metadata omit a test. An
unregistered ordinary unit or source-only E2E spec is valid and is still found
by the runners and recursive TEST-INDEX guard. No central registration is needed
unless it joins a curated tier/profile or requires historical/prerequisite
handling. Target-sensitive tests missing applicable membership must fail the
membership guard; absence of metadata must not be interpreted as source-only.

For mixed-profile specs, compare declared profiles with existing target
branches/helpers and runtime discovery/skip evidence. Do not add a second
manually enumerated case database. Require explicit supported declarations for
target-sensitive cases; dynamic/unresolvable branches fail for review rather
than silently count as covered. A non-source-only case must actually be selected
by an applicable runnable profile, proven with an omitted-membership fault.
Discovery/list output proves selection only, not execution, non-skip status,
assertion reachability or server identity. The prototype must capture a runtime
report for the exact case and make a deliberate target-branch fault fail that
same case before the manifest is accepted as the right design.

### 4.4 Static Counts Versus Runtime Discovery (T9)

Retain the existing AST-based tripwire and compare both supported assertion
and test-declaration CallExpression counts per file. These are static call
sites, not discovered/executed cases: a declaration inside a loop counts once,
whether the matrix generates one case or nine. Document supported declaration
forms; do not imply the current scanner recognizes every parameterization API.

Keep runtime discovery/execution counts separately in run receipts, labelled
by profile and selection. Do not compare static counts with runtime counts or
add a mandatory runtime-count baseline as part of T9. Shrinking a matrix can
lose cases without changing either static count; profile membership checks,
review of matrix edits and meaningful fault tests supply different evidence.

A legitimate refactor from several declarations into one parameterized loop
may lower static counts. Require a recorded reason, reviewed before/after case
selection and preserved assertion/fault evidence rather than automatic rejection
or silent re-baselining. Such an alert is an intentional tripwire, not proof
that coverage regressed. If known counting syntax cannot represent a refactor,
report that limitation explicitly instead of declaring equivalence from counts.

### 4.5 Shared Discovery And Parsing, Separate Policies

The recursive index guard, skip audit, assertion-count tripwire and later
membership guard must consume one neutral inventory of repository-relative spec
paths. The skip and count checks should also share TypeScript transformation,
AST parsing and tree-walking mechanics. Do not copy another directory walker,
comment stripper or parser bootstrap into each test.

Keep policy evaluation separate after that shared input: index completeness,
skip classification, assertion/declaration counts and profile membership answer
different questions and must continue to fail independently. The shared helper
does not resolve aliases beyond the documented grammar, interpret test meaning,
or become a generalized JavaScript analyzer. Active, historical, fixture and
support roots remain explicit inputs so sharing discovery cannot silently widen
a release suite.

Do not collapse checks that only appear similar. Static skip auditing and runtime
skip reconciliation cover different failure modes; `forbidOnly` is a runtime
backstop, not a replacement. `TEST-INDEX.md` documents every spec, while the
manifest governs only curated membership. Assertion-count baselines detect lost
call sites, not missing documentation. Repeating a case on web, portable,
portable-http or another browser is kept only when the case names an
environment-dependent failure it can catch there -- a download, crypto, file
access, PDF or canvas output, offline caching, or an engine-specific input or
focus behavior. Otherwise a rule is proven once at its cheapest reliable layer,
with representative browser wiring kept; cross-profile repetition with no named
environment risk is duplication (2026-10-13, after Codex's efficiency review).

## 5. Retained Principles And Future Coverage Backlog

The following guides tests when relevant to approved changes. It does not
require a new property/journey/accessibility/security/performance program to
complete T1-T11 remediation. N1's bounded fixture/preflight contract is the
specific required addition in Delivery 3; broader fixture expansion remains a
backlog. Retain strong existing checks; each new coverage
item needs a demonstrated gap, scoped file list, independent expected result,
cost estimate and individual approval. No minimum new-test count or all-form
coverage expansion is an initial acceptance criterion.

### 5.1 Fixtures And Isolation

Retain minimal-valid overlays and variant generators. Provide fresh per-form
blank, minimal-valid, populated, invalid, boundary, legacy and hostile fixtures.
Validate completeness against real validators and row factories; synthetic
saturation is not a realistic valid filing.

A fixture described as valid, populated, placement-only or positive-path must
pass the current field-domain rules and the real output preflight before the
action under test. Constrained paths use a value from their actual domain:
Florida county, enum option, tri-state value, valid date/range, identifier shape
or other applicable constraint. A generic `text`/number probe must not populate
a constrained path merely because the destination cell accepts text or a number.
Prefer the smallest explicit/domain-aware builder operation over embedding a
second copy of the product validator in test code.

When requiredness, normalization, enum membership, field-domain validation or
an output blocker changes, audit every affected minimal-valid base, overlay,
manifest builder and sibling fixture—not only fixtures missing a newly required
field. Run the relevant fixture contract before waiting for downstream artifact
generation.

Positive export helpers default to `allowed`: they inspect real preflight/UI
state and fail immediately with the visible issue text if output is blocked or
unexpectedly requires acknowledgement. Tests intentionally exercising invalid
or bypassable output must opt into the expected gate state and drive the real
acknowledgement control. Arm a download wait only after those preconditions are
established; if a visible blocker/prompt appears after the click, surface it
instead of consuming the full download timeout.

Correcting invalid fixture data does not close a distinct product defect exposed
by that data. Preserve a minimal reproduction and add a separately scoped,
red-first regression for the observable behavior. In the 2026-10-07 example,
re-entering Preview must leave Save as Excel either able to download or visibly
requiring acknowledgement; an enabled control that silently redraws Preview is
never an acceptable third state.

Use synthetic identities and sensitive-looking data only. Separate builders,
actions, inspectors and assertions. Adapters may seed unrelated setup; actions
under test use real controls. Isolate contexts/storage/downloads and control
IDs/time/random seeds where useful; retain real crypto/browser integration tests.

### 5.2 Rules And Contracts

Cover blank versus zero, permitted negatives and invalid numbers, percentage
limits, half-cent boundaries, date order, collection minimum/maximum and one
beyond output capacity, and each required field independently missing.
Use seeded properties for normalization, non-destructive toggles, persistence
and applicable carry/reset rules; record failing seeds.

Explicit invariants:

- Unanswered is not No; hiding is not deletion.
- Automatic readiness corresponds to export validation errors; manual duties
  do not block. Sidebar prompts are separate, with intentional differences
  verified rather than erased.
- An unrepresented filing must not acquire attorney-certification blockers.
- An acknowledgement keeps issues visible and output faithful; integrity,
  capacity and generation failures remain non-bypassable.
- Test capacity against the applicable output format, not every export by assumption.

### 5.3 Independent Artifact Evidence

Inspect actual workbooks through structured parsers/object models. Check typed
values against reviewed expected addresses and preserve formulas, merged-cell
masters, names, sheet order, print-area indices, header propagation and capacity.
Round trips are additional evidence, never the sole oracle.

Formula presence is not evaluated-number correctness. Use reviewed court
examples and a trusted spreadsheet application's calculation/rendering for
representative cases; record engine/version and approved differences. Do not
invent a substitute calculation engine as legal authority.

Check PDF text, identity, figures, signatures, masking, page/attachment order
and representative renders, including long content and clipping. Normalize
irrelevant metadata, not filed values. Review baselines against authority,
not just current output. Cross-form changes require AGENTS' sibling/template
reads; discovery does not authorize fixing every sibling defect.

### 5.4 Journeys And Specialist Coverage

Critical journeys: create/enter/save/reopen/export; workbook import/edit/output;
encrypted backup/restore and wrong password/corruption; rollover/conversion;
merge then reopen historical filings; draft/navigation/lock/recovery; hosted
offline/update/reload with retained data.

Parameterize shared rules over all filing identities at the cheapest reliable
layer, usually a unit test. Browser and artifact suites cover each distinct
wiring or output implementation, not every identity automatically: the
Inventory, the Annual family and the Simplified often implement a concept
separately (AGENTS.md section 8, item 9) and need their own browser case, while
Annual, Final and Trust share an engine and need identity assertions rather than
a full repeated interaction sequence (2026-10-13, after Codex's efficiency review). Use representative pairwise
browser/environment coverage with mandatory combinations for crypto, downloads,
PDF/canvas, offline and file access. Unsupported combinations need reasons.

Accessibility: labels/roles, errors/announcements, keyboard/focus, dialogs,
contrast/zoom/narrow viewports, manual screen-reader review and PDF accessibility.
Security: tamper rejection, hostile inputs, unwanted plaintext storage/logging
or transmission; do not imply encryption secures a compromised unlocked device.
Performance: startup, route cycles, mount/dispose growth and large synthetic
files on identified hardware/filesystems, with measured budgets.

### 5.5 Keeping The Suite Lean

*Added 2026-10-13, after Codex's efficiency review.* A new browser matrix -- a
loop generating cases over forms, targets or browsers -- states in its spec or
`TEST-INDEX.md` row the observable failure it catches, why a unit or focused
contract cannot, its generated case count and approximate time, and which
forms, targets or browsers genuinely differ. Overlap with an existing case is
removed or justified. Consolidation that lowers static counts is permitted with
a recorded reason and preserved fault evidence (4.4); a falling count is never a
reason to keep a redundant case.

## 6. Execution Tiers And Permissions

| Selection | Contents | Permission And Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Individual sub-test | Named case/parameter plus setup/prerequisites | Diagnosis/red-first; not whole-module coverage. |
| Focused module | Affected rules/contracts and consumer UI/artifact checks | Default development evidence; expand through dependencies. |
| Quick | Fast units/infrastructure plus critical browser smoke | Convenience, not full regression or release proof. |
| Full source | Active units and complete source/Chromium E2E | Explicit approval; preserve `npm test` meaning. |
| Verify | Types/data model followed by full source | Explicit approval under current policy. |
| Release | Types/data model/units, full source once, curated distribution/browser legs | Release authorization; not every case on every browser. |
| Scheduled/specialist | Migration corpus, properties/faults/stress/performance/manual checks | Approved scope, frequency, budget and prerequisites. |
| Historical | Archived comparison/workflow on its recorded source | Explicit on-demand execution; not a current gate. |

Keep fail-fast prerequisites and serial browser execution until measurements
justify isolated parallelism. Delivery 1M takes that measurement: Milestone
59's light-spec probe already halved its specs' time at four workers, and the
heavy specs are unprobed (section 2.3). Built profiles build their own artifacts; do not
prepend redundant builds or duplicate full source in release composition.
Keep failure traces/artifacts; retries must not erase first-run flakes.

The runner's `all` operation must enumerate an explicit release-profile list;
it must never mean “every key in the profile registry.” Quick, focused,
historical, diagnostic and future specialist entries are excluded unless a
separate approved change deliberately adds one to the release list. Full source
already contains the quick browser cases, so release must not run quick again.

Keep one implementation behind each command family. `test:e2e:source` owns the
source-runner invocation and `test:e2e` is a compatibility alias used by the
unchanged `npm test` composition. Add a browser-only `test:e2e:quick`; compose
`test:quick` as unit plus `test:e2e:quick`. Automation that already ran units
calls `test:e2e:quick`, not `test:quick`, so units execute once. The four quick
spec paths have one owner, initially the fixed runner entry and later the
accepted manifest; package scripts contain no copied path list.

Recommended automation split, subject to delivery 5 approval:

- **Automatic lightweight feedback:** type check, data-model verification,
  unit tests and `test:e2e:quick`. Do not call the composite `test:quick` after
  running units separately.
- **Human-authorized/manual dispatch:** full source and release matrix, with
  explicit dispatch permissions and recorded requester approval.
- **Scheduled or manually triggered:** historical corpus, performance, stress,
  specialist and migration comparisons under separately approved budgets.

Publish receipts/logs as workflow artifacts with retention limits; do not
commit generated run results. Automatic full-source or release triggers are
not proposed. Recommendation does not authorize pipeline/hooks/protection.
If automation is deferred, label enforcement manual/external and identify
its receipts; do not retain a fictional CI guarantee.

## 7. Future AGENTS Testing Protocol

Integrate this method into AGENTS only after implementation verifies its
commands/guards. Until then, current AGENTS governs.

This section is candidate source text, not a second permanent policy manual.
After the relevant deliveries land, move only verified rules into AGENTS and
mark this section historical/implemented. README remains orientation and
HOW-TO-RUN remains command guidance; neither should independently restate test
permissions or profile membership. Where repetition is useful for a reader,
link to the authoritative rule instead of maintaining parallel normative text.

### 7.1 Before Testing

1. Read AGENTS and manifest/index; inspect status/history and concurrent edits.
   Sync safely under repo rules, not by merging/stashing others' dirty work.
2. State observable behavior, affected forms/contracts, reference provenance
   when relevant, and cheapest falsifying check.
3. Inspect affected modules and shared consumers; list selected cases/paths/
   targets, prerequisites and estimated cost. Changed-file suggestions are
   advisory, not a complete dependency map or proof that omitted tests are safe.
4. Select layers below; ask immediately when scope, legal interpretation,
   compatibility, or expensive execution needs a decision.
5. Verify checkout/build identity, target/browser, owned server and discovery.
   Missing prerequisites/expected cases fail; do not silently switch browser,
   reuse stale servers or skip required coverage.

### 7.2 Instructions For Each Test Type

| Change/Test Type | Required Testing And Sub-Testing |
| --- | --- |
| Documentation only | Validate paths, command claims, indexes and permission consistency; no product tests. |
| Pure rule/calculator/model | Named unit case during development, then relevant owning specs and boundaries; independent expectations. New property coverage requires scoped approval. |
| Shared service/contract | Focused integration success/failure cases then all consumer contracts; mock outer effects only. |
| Fixture/factory/helper | Positive fixtures use domain-valid values and pass real validators/preflight; constrained paths never receive generic probes. Invalid fixtures declare their expected issue/gate. Async helpers assert visible preconditions before long event waits and surface blockers immediately. |
| Field/card/page | Real input/click/keyboard, commit, validation, hide/restore, add/remove/re-index and relevant form variants; then feature contracts. |
| Navigation/lifecycle | Transitions, cancellation/disposal, draft commit, active identity and recovery, plus changed-transition journey. |
| Persisted shape/migration | CSV verification, fixture/factory audit, save/load, legacy corpus, loss/ambiguity/error visibility and affected import/export. |
| Save/encryption/recovery | Real persistence/crypto, wrong-password/tamper/storage errors, UI backup/restore/recovery and affected browser/target branches. |
| Validation/readiness | Missing-field/boundary/no-op cases, county/form rules, no attorney, readiness/sidebar differences, acknowledgement and non-bypassable output. Any requiredness/domain/enum/blocker change triggers the affected fixture/factory audit. |
| Excel/PDF/import/export | Model/placement checks plus actual generated artifact; capacity/signature/attachment/overflow branches; round-trip additional only. Positive helpers require an allowed preflight before arming download waits; invalid/override flows opt in and drive real controls. |
| Styling/accessibility | Desktop/narrow/zoom/theme, real keyboard/focus/errors, rendered geometry and manual screen-reader review when semantics change. |
| Packaging/offline/update | Target-runner build, hosted and portable file/subfolder checks, cache/update/assets and download/output smoke; recommend portable E2E explicitly. |
| Runner/manifest/governance | Conflicting env, wrong/busy server, missing/duplicate/nested specs, unknown profiles, omitted branches, forbidden modifiers/skips, count drops and archive leakage; real child exit propagation. |
| Performance/lifecycle | Identified controlled environment, repeated baseline/comparison, budget and variance; not a correctness substitute. |
| Characterization/golden | Separate historical from normative behavior; review values and provenance; explain updates, never regenerate just for green. |
| Mutation/fault injection | Wrong sign/cell, omitted write, lost link, hidden control or coerced answer; intended test detects fault; restore probe and rerun clean. |
| Manual/exploratory/reference | Record checklist, authority, environment, observations/reviewer; distinguish output verification from legal interpretation. |
| Historical replay | Isolated recorded source/config/dependencies; report historical evidence, not release proof; stop on unavailable prerequisites. |

### 7.3 Selecting Cases And Modules

Before delivery 1, current narrow templates must pin both environment values.
Use an actual spec/case. Preserve and restore the caller's environment even on
failure; capture the child exit code separately from restoration:

```powershell
npx vitest run tests/unit/<spec>.spec.js -t "<case name>"
npx vitest run tests/unit/<spec>.spec.js

$previousTarget = $env:PG_TARGET
$previousBrowser = $env:PG_BROWSER
$testExitCode = 1
try {
   $env:PG_TARGET = 'source'
   $env:PG_BROWSER = 'chromium'
   npx playwright test tests/e2e/<spec>.spec.ts --grep "<case name>"
   $testExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
} finally {
   $env:PG_TARGET = $previousTarget
   $env:PG_BROWSER = $previousBrowser
}
if ($testExitCode -ne 0) { throw "Playwright failed with exit code $testExitCode" }
```

For the whole browser spec, omit `--grep`. Placeholders are not runnable paths.
`--project=chromium` alone cannot select Chromium when `PG_BROWSER` created only
a Firefox project. Pin both values in the process that launches Playwright.
These interim commands still have T2's server-reuse risk; they do not establish
trustworthy verification until that repair lands. Do not claim otherwise.

After delivery 1, standard named tiers use the repaired existing profile runner
through fixed package commands:

```powershell
npm run test:e2e:source
npm run test:e2e:quick  # browser smoke only; useful after units already ran
npm run test:quick
# npm test remains the full source regression and still requires approval.
```

Focused cases continue to use the explicitly pinned direct Playwright template
above. Delivery 1 does not add positional spec paths, `--grep` forwarding,
`--list` mode, generic module selection or a second wrapper. Its runner tests
verify fixed source and quick composition, environment ownership, nonempty quick
selection and child failure propagation. A maintainer may use a direct pinned
Playwright `--list` command as a diagnostic, but that is not a new runner API or
execution proof. Never use `.only` for selection. Add named-tier examples to
AGENTS only after their focused tests pass.

### 7.4 Regression Proof And Completion

1. Establish red for the stated bug, then green with the fix. Follow scoped
   stash proof only for task-owned files while keeping regression tests available
   for red. If edits are mixed with concurrent work, agree isolated-worktree/probe
   verification rather than hiding somebody else's changes. Stash only between
   browser runs, never during one: the source target serves the working tree,
   so a running suite would test the stashed tree (2026-10-12 recheck, section 2.2).
2. Immediately after the first substantive edit, run the smallest executable
   check; repair that slice before expanding. Then run module/consumer selections.
3. Run scoped `check:types` and `verify:data-model` when required; validate
   fixture/index/profile ownership changes and update TEST-INDEX/file_index.
4. For a requiredness/domain/enum/output-blocker change, audit affected positive
   fixtures and prove their expected real preflight state. Before an async output
   wait, assert the action is currently permitted or the declared negative gate
   is visible; fail with that issue rather than timing out.
5. If correcting test setup exposes a separate product failure, preserve its
   minimal reproduction and disposition it independently; do not let the fixture
   correction silently erase the product defect.
6. Use bounded observable waits; document negative windows and assert absence.
7. Skips need capability, environment or temporary-gap classification and reason.
   Temporary gaps require owner/real issue/expiry. Environment failures/gaps
   cannot satisfy release coverage without recorded acceptance. Historical
   prerequisite exclusions belong in their separate workflow.
8. Recommend full regression for cross-cutting changes and portable checks for
   packaging; obtain approval. Quick success is not full-regression evidence.
9. Report command/filter, source/dirty overlay, build/target/browser,
   discovered/executed/passed/failed/skipped/retried counts, time, evidence,
   red-first result and unexecuted coverage. List-only and historical runs are
   never reported as product regression passes. A first unit run that fails
   whole files on load or file-scan timeouts beside or just after a browser
   run, and passes on rerun, is reported as a retry (2026-10-12 recheck, section 2.2).

## 8. Selective Historical Preservation

### 8.1 Preserve The Suite Without Duplicating It

Do not copy the full tests, fixtures, baselines, scripts, lockfile, configs and
docs into this repository. That inflates inventory/searches and creates a
permanent exclusion burden. Preserve the committed suite with an agreed,
verified commit reference and, if explicitly authorized, a descriptive tag.
Do not create a tag or commit as part of this planning task.

Provide an accessible small catalogue under `archive/testing/` when delivery 7
is approved:

```text
archive/testing/
  README.md                  # how to browse/retrieve the historical suite
  suite-reference.json       # verified commit/tag, paths and prerequisites
  retired-tools/             # only approved, operationally useful retired tools
```

The concise reference identifies original test/process/config/doc directories,
verified SHA/tag, tool and lockfile versions, known limitations and replay steps.
Explain retrieval through Git and a repository-host commit view for readers
who do not use Git. Keep ledgers/proposals readable in their existing locations.
Git preserves removed guard implementations; do not copy an unusable guard
into retired-tools solely because it was deleted.

If the intended audience needs a full snapshot without Git, separately approve
an external zip/bundle location outside the active repository. Record its
checksum, source identity, access/retention policy and retrieval link in the
catalogue. Exclude secrets, real filer data, dependencies/builds and uncontrolled
traces. Do not claim external preservation until retrieval has been verified.

### 8.2 Stable Reference And Replay

1. Agree a clean committed capture point after coordinating concurrent work.
   The tree is now clean and level with origin; `a5833f5`, where the
   2026-10-12 full regression passed, is a candidate (2026-10-12 recheck, section 2.2). Record existing process
   instructions and known audit defects without falsely presenting them as repaired.
2. Verify the SHA/tag and the historical test/process paths it resolves. This
   small reference operation does not block execution fixes or require full tests.
3. Retrieve into an isolated checkout using the recorded lockfile/toolchain
   and original paths. Archived tests depend on matching production source.
4. Verify representative retrieval/discovery and, if approved, focused replay.
   Ask before historical full regression; report unavailable dependencies.
5. Keep historical receipts distinct from current release evidence. Rollback
   is a reviewed restoration from the verified revision, never a dirty-tree reset.

### 8.3 Selective Retirement Rules

Remove T8's unusable ledger script/unit spec from active tooling during
delivery 2 while preserving its history in Git and its ledger in place.
Separate pre-merge comparison as an explicitly on-demand workflow; keep it
operational if its comparison still serves a documented purpose. Review the
declaration-disposition test in its own scope. Keep live architecture ratchets.

Only place tools in retired-tools when genuinely retired, useful to the intended
audience, and not adequately accessible through the catalogue/history. Each
gets a short purpose, original path/revision, prerequisites, limitations and
explicit non-gate status. Exclude that small area from discovery and ensure
no active process imports it. Update file_index and TEST-INDEX for approved
additions/moves/deletions; archive entries are not active coverage.

Do not retire a useful regression without identifying its retained/replacement
checks and fault evidence. Do not demand successors for branch-specific obsolete
workflows or vacuous assertions. No wholesale archive or migration is proposed.

## 9. Bounded Delivery Sequence

All paths below are scoped candidates based on current code. New paths are
explicitly marked proposed. Before requesting implementation approval, check
concurrent edits, confirm imports/callers and finalize the exact file list.
If additional files are needed, surface that scope change before editing.
Runtime ranges are planning estimates for targeted checks, not measured
promises; remeasure on this workstation. Full regression is excluded from
these estimates and always needs explicit approval.

**Recommended immediate authorization:** approve Delivery 1 only, limited to
the vacuous backup regression, fixed source/Chromium named tiers, nonduplicating
package aliases, an explicit release sequence that excludes quick/diagnostic/
historical entries, refusal of unknown servers, focused runner tests and matching
documentation. Do not treat that approval as authorization for a general
selection/list interface, interactive reuse, identity stamps, custom process
management, fixture/export-helper changes, a manifest, Deliveries 2-7, or
full/portable regression. Request any
expansion separately.

### Delivery 1: Truthful Execution (T3, T1, T2, T11)

**Files:** `tests/e2e/verified-inventory-workflow.spec.ts`,
`scripts/run-e2e-profile.mjs`, `playwright.config.ts`, `package.json`,
`README.md`, `HOW-TO-RUN.txt`, `TEST-INDEX.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `file_index.md`;
proposed `tests/unit/test-profile-runner.spec.js` for child/config tests.
Update existing profile comments/help strings in the runner/config; defer
shared vocabulary extraction to delivery 4, not another wrapper.

**Checks:** the backup-event case, `tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts`, and the proposed
runner spec. Route `npm test`'s browser leg through the existing fixed source
profile and give the four quick browser specs a fixed source/Chromium entry in
that runner. Add browser-only `test:e2e:quick`; make `test:quick` compose unit
plus that command without copying spec paths into `package.json`. Keep
`test:e2e:source` as the single source-run implementation and `test:e2e` as its
compatibility alias so `npm test` retains its existing composition. Test those
named-tier/alias compositions, conflicting-environment override, nonempty quick
selection, unknown profile input and child failure propagation. Replace `all`'s
`Object.keys(PROFILES)` behavior with an explicit release sequence and prove each
existing release profile runs once while quick is excluded. Preserve existing
built-profile behavior; do not redesign it here.

**Faults:** hide Save Backup; conflicting target/browser variables; unrelated
server on the configured port; failing Playwright child; empty fixed quick
selection; quick or a synthetic diagnostic entry accidentally included in `all`.
Assert that the busy-port error names the profile/port, provides safe inspection
guidance and leaves the foreign process untouched. Check cleanup of an owned
server through Playwright's ordinary lifecycle after success and child failure,
and keep startup collisions after preflight fatal, with Playwright's own
"already used" failure followed by the same port-inspection guidance (3.1).
Restore probes and establish
the stated red/green results.

**Explicitly out of scope:** a generic spec/case/`--grep`/`--list` command-line
interface; interactive server reuse; checkout/build identity stamps or
handshakes; custom signal forwarding, process-tree killing or interruption
management; shared manifest/vocabulary extraction; generic module selection;
and any Delivery 2-7 work. Surface any claimed need for one of these as a scope
change before editing.

**Estimated check time:** 5-15 minutes including focused browser/fault reruns
and the server-collision probe; no implementation-time promise.
**Approval:** focused checks are the default. Recommend/request full source
because runner semantics are shared; request portable approval if portable
execution/build behavior changes. Do not run either unprompted.

**Exit:** named full-source and quick tiers truthfully select this working
directory's source/Chromium, verification refuses unknown servers, missing backup
action fails, release runs no quick/diagnostic/historical entry, and command/
profile/permission/CI claims match reality. Package aliases contain no duplicate
spec lists. The existing browser runner owns those fixed entries without becoming
a general test selector.

### Build record — BUILT 2026-10-13, `4f6b864` (approved by the requester 2026-10-13: "Implement TEST-REVIEW.md", all deliveries in order)

**What a maintainer sees:** `npm test` and `npm run test:quick` test this
working tree on source/Chromium whatever `PG_TARGET` or `PG_BROWSER` the
shell carries: both go through `scripts/run-e2e-profile.mjs` (`test:e2e` is
its `source` profile; the new `test:e2e:quick` is its `quick` profile, the
four smoke specs owned there and no longer copied into `package.json`;
`test:quick` is unit + `test:e2e:quick`; `npm test`'s composition is
unchanged). A profile refuses to start while the port its server needs is
held, naming the profile, the URL and port, that nothing was reused or
stopped, and the PowerShell commands to see what holds it; the port comes
from `playwright.config.ts`, which exports its `TARGETS` table and never
reuses a listening server (`reuseExistingServer` was `!CI`). Playwright's
own late "is already used" error gets the same guidance. `all` runs an
explicit list of seven release profiles, never `quick`. The Inventory's
save-event test, which had passed without clicking anything (the Save
Backup button sits in the save controls, collapsed by default, and `if
(await saveBtn.isVisible())` skipped the whole test), opens the controls,
requires the button and asserts the event. README, HOW-TO-RUN, TEST-INDEX
and AGENTS.md say what the commands do; TEST-INDEX no longer requires a
full `npm test` before every commit, and its pdf-export row names
`schedule-card-layout` (T7's stale `attestation-layout` reference, a
documentation fix taken here).

**Where the build differs from the design, and why:**

- The runner reads each target's port from `playwright.config.ts` by
  importing it (Node strips the types; `TARGETS` is a new named export) --
  the config stays the one owner of server URLs, and no vocabulary was
  extracted (deferred to Delivery 4).
- The runner now pipes Playwright's output through itself, forwarding it as
  it arrives, so it can recognise the late collision text. Playwright's list
  reporter therefore prints its non-TTY form (one line per test as it
  finishes) -- the form every logged run already showed.
- The one real child in the unit spec is `node -e process.exit(3)`; every
  Playwright launch in the spec is a fake that records what it would have
  run. The real launches are the browser probes below.
- No signal forwarding, process-tree killing, orphan reclamation or
  interactive reuse (out of scope, as the delivery says). The port probe
  checks both loopback addresses because `vite preview` binds `::1` only
  here (`run-guide-capture.mjs` found the same and keeps its own copy of the
  probe; the two can share once that script is next touched).

### Delivery 1M: Measured Minimization (Run Time)

*Added 2026-10-13 at the requester's decision, after Codex's efficiency review:
a measured cut in run time is a completion requirement (section 10). Section
2.3 holds the evidence.*

**Approval gate:** after Delivery 1, whose pinned, owned-server runner makes
timings trustworthy. Request it separately with its exact file list and probes;
any full regression it needs is approved on its own.

**Measure first:**

1. *Per-case setup cost.* Time the shared setup helpers
   (`freshStartNoPassword()`, `createWard()`, the `fillMinimalValid*()`
   fixtures, the first navigation) across a representative sample of specs in
   a focused run on C:, and report what share of the 2.6-second floor they
   are.
2. *The heavy-spec parallel probe* Milestone 59 left undone: the PDF, Excel,
   download, offline-cache and cross-tab specs at two to four workers, three
   runs each, on C:. Each run needs its own owned server; Delivery 1's server
   ownership is the prerequisite.
3. *A current baseline:* per-spec times from the 2026-10-12 log, recorded as
   dated evidence (proposed `tests/baseline/runtime-2026-10-12.json`), with
   each profile's selected, executed and skipped counts and the builds per
   release.
4. *A redundancy audit by proof role* over the thirty slowest specs (54% of
   the time) and the extra-browser list. For each repeated scenario, name what
   it proves: rule correctness (belongs exhaustively in a unit test), UI wiring
   (one case per distinct renderer or adapter), artifact correctness (one

   compatibility (only where the environment can change behavior), or a

**Then reduce,** each change separately approved and fault-proven:

**Target:** set by the requester from the measurements above, in minutes of
full-source wall time on C:.

**Estimated check time:** each probe about 10-20 minutes. The 2026-10-12 run

**Exit:** a before/after full-source measurement on C:, on the same machine,

**Files:** `tests/unit/test-index-guard.spec.js`,

`tests/e2e/pre-merge-output.characterization.spec.ts`,
`scripts/ms70-assertion-counts.mjs`, `tests/unit/ms70-assertion-counts.spec.js`,
proposed `scripts/test-source-analysis.mjs` for neutral recursive discovery,
TypeScript transformation, parsing and AST walking,
`scripts/run-e2e-profile.mjs`, `playwright.config.ts`, `package.json`,
`TEST-INDEX.md`, `file_index.md` and relevant AGENTS governance instructions.
Delete `scripts/ms70-ledger-guard.mjs` and `tests/unit/ms70-ledger-guard.spec.js`.
Proposed targeted move to `tests/historical/pre-merge-output.characterization.spec.ts`
and proposed `playwright.historical.config.ts`; the existing runner selects
that config explicitly, not a new wrapper. Fix relative imports if moved.
Keep `MILESTONE-70-FIX-LEDGER.md` unchanged and readable.

**Parser boundary:** use the repository's existing AST tooling rather than
regular expressions. Support direct imports of the Vitest/Playwright test APIs,
ordinary renamed import aliases, whitespace/nesting, and documented property
chains such as `test.skip`, `test.fixme`, `test.only`, `test.describe.skip` and
`test.describe.only`. Do not attempt assignment tracking, arbitrary wrappers,
re-exports, computed property names or dynamically constructed test APIs. When
a call looks disable-related but cannot be resolved within the supported grammar,
fail with its file/location and require review or an explicit supported form.
Enable Playwright's runtime `forbidOnly` protection (or the verified equivalent)
as a backstop; it does not replace the recursive audit.

The proposed shared source-analysis helper contains mechanics only: explicit-root
recursive path discovery, OXC TypeScript transformation, Acorn parsing and AST
walking. The index, skip and count guards import those mechanics but retain
separate policy functions and failure messages. Do not make the index guard
depend on skip/count policy, or combine their baselines and acceptance rules.

**Checks:** the touched governance unit specs, plus focused runner checks
for the new on-demand historical entry and failure propagation. Direct discovery
with the historical config proves default/full profiles do not include the
pre-merge workflow while the historical config still finds it; this does not add
a generic runner list interface. Prove the explicit `all` sequence also excludes
the historical entry. Fault the shared inventory once and show each consuming
guard receives the same recursive repository-relative paths while failing on its
own rule. Update count baselines only for approved
deletions/moves, with reasons and preserved historical reference, never blanket reset.

**Faults:** nested and TypeScript specs, duplicate basenames/rows, stale selection
references, direct-import aliases, spaced/nested/describe-level skip/only/fixme,
an ambiguous computed or reassigned API that produces a review diagnostic,
invalid temporary-gap reference, removed declaration with unchanged assertion
count, and historical workflow leaking into active discovery.
Include a loop whose matrix size changes while static counts stay constant,
and a multi-declaration-to-loop refactor with a justified count drop. Assert
static semantics and reason handling; do not label static counts runtime coverage.

**Estimated check time:** 2-10 minutes for targeted units/discovery. A historical
runtime comparison may need builds and retrieval, estimated separately.
**Approval:** finalize the exact grammar and file list from Delivery 1 evidence,
then request Delivery 2 separately. No full/source/portable run is planned;
request one only if results show broader selection changes. Historical runtime
comparison needs separately agreed SHA/prerequisites and cost. T10 cleanup is
not a delivery gate.

**Exit:** guards match recursive discovery and detect their synthetic faults;
supported syntax is documented, ambiguous syntax is surfaced rather than guessed,
one neutral inventory/parser implementation feeds separate policies, historical
execution remains outside release, obsolete tooling is no longer live, and
preserved useful ratchets are unaffected.
