### Delivery 3: Fixture Contracts And Fail-Fast Output Preconditions (N1)

**Files** (the Milestone 74 work this waited on has landed, 2026-10-12 recheck, section 2.2):
`tests/e2e/support/export-manifests.ts`,
`tests/e2e/support/workbook-vs-template.ts`,
`tests/e2e/support/fixture-completeness.ts`,
`tests/e2e/excel-form-field-placement.spec.ts`, the existing acknowledgement
unit/E2E specs that actually own the lifecycle, `TEST-INDEX.md`, `AGENTS.md` and
`file_index.md`. `output-buttons-after-override.spec.ts` owns the Preview
re-entry behavior since `a0e987b`, and `exportWithWrites()` already checks
readiness before its download wait; what remains is the fixture-validity
half -- a positive helper that fails when an override is needed, with
overriding an explicit opt-in (2026-10-12 recheck, section 2.2).

**Fixture contract:** positive/minimal-valid/populated/placement fixtures must
pass the current validators and real output preflight with the expected filing
identity. Constrained fields use domain-valid values, not generic probe strings.
Invalid, boundary and override fixtures remain valuable but declare the exact
expected issue and gate state so they cannot be mistaken for positive setup.
Do not duplicate product validation logic inside the fixture builder.

**Output-helper contract:** default positive export helpers require an `allowed`
preflight before arming `page.waitForEvent('download')`. If the page is blocked or
unexpectedly requests acknowledgement, fail immediately with the visible issue
text and expected/actual gate state. An explicit option may request
`acknowledgement-required`; that path must click the real control, confirm the
dialog and then prove the download. A visible blocker/prompt after the export
click must win a race against the download wait and produce the diagnostic rather
than a long timeout.

**Checks:** focused fixture/preflight checks for each affected filing family,
the workbook-placement case that exposed N1, the output-helper contract, and the
acknowledgement lifecycle regression. Run `check:types` because the candidate
support files are in TypeScript's checked scope. Do not turn this delivery into
validation of every historical/negative fixture in the repository.

**Faults:** replace a valid positive county with `V0010` and confirm immediate
failure naming the county/preflight issue before any download wait; restore a
real Florida county and reach the downloaded workbook assertions. Mark the same
invalid fixture as an expected acknowledgement case and prove the real override
path still works. Reproduce the separate enabled-but-nonfunctional Save as Excel
state after Preview re-entry: the test fails unless the click downloads or a
visible acknowledgement request replaces the enabled state (done by
`output-buttons-after-override.spec.ts` since `a0e987b`; keep it as an
existing check, 2026-10-12 recheck, section 2.2). Restore all probes
and record red/green evidence for the reason claimed.

**Estimated check time:** measure now that its Milestone 74 part has landed.
Budget focused validator/
helper checks separately from workbook generation; the invalid-county fault must
fail in seconds rather than consume a 180-second download timeout.
**Approval:** request Delivery 3 separately with its exact file list.
No full/source/portable regression is implicit; recommend broader approval only
if shared fixture/helper changes affect consumers beyond the focused inventory.

**Exit:** positive fixtures cannot silently carry out-of-domain values into an
artifact test, export helpers report gate failures before long event waits,
intentional override cases remain explicit, and correcting a fixture cannot erase
a separately observed product defect without a retained regression/disposition.

### Delivery 4: Prototype, Then Minimal Profile Manifest (T5)

**Approval gate:** Delivery 4 is not ready for full implementation approval.
First request a separately bounded prototype (4P) after Delivery 3 and after
Delivery 1M's consolidations, so the manifest records the reduced matrices
rather than today's (2026-10-13). Use the
existing web-only case `failed feature chunk shows a reload action instead of a
blank view (web, hashed build)` as the concrete probe unless intervening changes
make another case materially simpler. The 4P request must name its exact files,
build command, runtime selection and estimated cost before work begins.

The prototype succeeds only if all of the following are demonstrated and saved
as reviewable evidence:

1. With membership present, a runtime reporter identifies that exact case as
   selected, completed and passed under the web target; skipped or merely listed
   does not count.
2. A reversible deliberate fault at a web-only assertion makes that exact case
   fail for the intended reason, proving the target-specific assertion path ran;
   restoring the probe returns it to green.
3. Removing the case/spec's web membership makes the proposed governance check
   fail before the product run, and restoring membership returns it to green.
4. An ordinary source-only spec that is present in `TEST-INDEX.md` but absent
   from the manifest remains discoverable and accepted, proving the mechanism
   does not turn full source into a manifest allowlist.

If 4P cannot establish all four without broad registration or a second case
database, revise or abandon the manifest design rather than expanding it by
default. Successful 4P evidence permits a request for the full delivery; it does
not itself authorize that delivery. The prototype uses the existing product case;
do not retain a copied case or a permanent probe-only runner. Preserve its command,
report and red/green result as evidence, then remove temporary fault hooks. Any
generally useful check becomes part of the membership/runner tests rather than a
second implementation of the same case.

lightweight job, dispatch authorization, receipt uploads/retention and clean-clone
reproduction. No full regression as a syntax-check side effect.
**Estimated check time:** provider validation plus one lightweight run; measure
that run rather than assigning inherited historical timings. Full/release
dispatch cost requires a separate approved run budget.
**Approval:** provider/triggers/permissions/cost decision first; human-authorized
full source and release only. Specialist schedules need their own approval.
**Exit:** documented enforcement and visible receipts match actual automation.

### Build record — BUILT 2026-10-15, `fb20e4ea` (the workflow and docs), `7c90b1bf` (the first run's measurement); the unit fixes the manual run found, `396e2a30`

**The one manual run (the plan's first step, approved by the requester
2026-10-15):** run 38725822122 on `b19d8392`, dispatched by hand. It
reached the unit step in 35 s (checkout, `npm ci` from cache, Chromium,
both builds, the Cloudflare assembly) and failed there after 2 min 15 s;
the Playwright steps were skipped. Three unit files failed:
`completion-parity.spec.js` and `validator-engines.spec.js` with
"planSimplified: variant 2: expected 'minimal valid' to be 'saturated'",
and `test-profile-runner.spec.js`'s "a real child exiting 3" with
`/bin/sh: 1: Syntax error: "(" unexpected` (exit 2). The log was the
result, as the plan said, and it said two things:

- The goldens were stale on every machine, not only Linux: Delivery 3 gave
  the three Plan identities minimal valid overlays, which changed the
  variants `tests/unit/support/filing-variants.js` yields, and nobody
  regenerated the goldens -- the full unit run here failed the same way.
  Fixed in `396e2a30`: regenerated with a note saying why (491 variants
  added, 518 "saturated" outcomes changed because the saturated filing is
  now built from the overlay, one label gone; no engine changed -- nothing
  under `src/` changed since the last green run; the other six types'
  3,046 variants compared equal to HEAD's per type and label).
- One test was shell-dependent: the runner spawns through the shell, and
  `sh` refuses a bare `(` where `cmd.exe` passes it on. Fixed in the test
  (`process.exitCode=3`), reproduced first under `bash -c` with the same
  error, and shown to return 3 under both `sh` and `cmd.exe`.

**The decision (the requester, 2026-10-15, from that evidence):**
provider GitHub Actions (already there; the repository is public, so
standard runners are free and unlimited -- GitHub's billing documentation
-- and the repository's default token permission was already read-only);
triggers: the lightweight check on every push to master touching
`probate-guardian/`, and a hand start offering `quick` or `source`;
nothing on a schedule; the release gate never runs there.

**What a maintainer sees:** a verdict on every push to master within the
15-minute limit -- type check, data model, the unit suite, both builds
with the Cloudflare assembly, then the quick browser tier on Linux
Chromium -- with the Playwright report and `test-results` kept 14 days as
the run's artifact. The whole source suite on Linux is one click away for
anyone with write access (Actions tab, `source`, 120-minute limit). A
newer push cancels the quick run before it; hand-started runs queue. The
workflow runs the repository's own commands (`npm run test:e2e:quick`,
`npm run test:e2e`) so the runner pins target and browser, never a bare
`npx playwright test` reading shell variables. Full history on checkout,
because the old-build comparisons and the archive catalogue read git.

**Checks and faults, as the plan listed them:**

- *Workflow syntax and permissions:* GitHub accepted the file on the push
  (an invalid file shows as a failed "Invalid workflow file" run; none);
  `permissions: contents: read` is explicit, and the repository's default
  is `read` (`actions/permissions/workflow`). No secrets, no deploy.
- *A deliberately failing lightweight job:* the manual run itself -- a red
  unit step made the job red and skipped every later step, which is the
  propagation the new workflow keeps (each step runs only after the one
  before it passed).
- *Dispatch authorization:* `workflow_dispatch` needs write access to the
  repository (GitHub's rule); the manual run was dispatched by the
  requester's account.
- *Receipt uploads and retention:* the first automatic run uploaded
  `quick-305` (241 KB) with `expires_at` 2026-10-29, fourteen days on;
  `if: always()` uploads on a red run too.
- *Clean-clone reproduction:* both runs are clean clones on GitHub's
  runner; the stale goldens reproduced there before they were fixed here.
- *No full regression as a side effect:* the push run executes 35 browser
  cases; the source job is gated on the hand-started choice and showed as
  not run.

**Measured, not inherited (run 38803541212 on `fb20e4ea`, the push that
added the trigger):** green in 5 min 24 s end to end -- checkout with
full history 6 s, Chromium 22 s, type check and data model about a second
each, unit suite 3 min 52 s, both builds and the assembly 3 s, the quick
browser tier 49 s, the upload 1 s. The old 15-minute limit holds this

**Where the build differs from the plan's candidate list:** `package.json`

**Not done, and why:** no scheduled run (the plan says a schedule needs
its own approval; the requester chose none); no release gate on Linux
(its Edge leg launches the system Edge and WebKit on Linux is a different

### Delivery 6: Optional Modularization And Coverage Backlog

Run-time reduction is no longer here: it is Delivery 1M, a completion
requirement (2026-10-13).

No fixed file list or required coverage program. Propose one measured maintenance
or coverage problem at a time, with exact paths, smallest test/fault check, runtime
budget and full/source/portable decision before approval. Start with optional tags;
move tests only when materially revised. Section 5 is a backlog, not this delivery's
blanket authorization. Optional work does not block protocol-remediation completion.

### Build record — BUILT 2026-10-15: item 1 `caca81b8`, item 2 `d3064f64`, item 3 `3be3bbc8` (each approved by the requester on 2026-10-15, proposed one at a time with its measurement)

The plan makes this delivery optional and item-by-item: a measured
maintenance or coverage problem, exact paths, the smallest check, a runtime
budget and the full/source/portable decision, then approval. Three were
proposed; all three were approved and built. Section 5 remains a backlog.

**Item 1 -- a fixture may write only keys its form has.** *What a
maintainer sees:* a typo'd or stray key in a positive fixture fails the
fixture contract at once, named with its form and path, instead of silently
filling nothing. *The measured problem:* since Delivery 3 the Plan for
Minors' minimal valid overlay carried `caseNumber`, a field that form does
not have (it keeps its Case # in `ref`); nothing read it, and it rode into
both goldens as two variants that meant nothing. No rule caught it: the
contract judged values against domains, never keys against the form.
*Built:* `tests/unit/fixture-contract.spec.js` -- a path is the form's when
its blank filing has it, or the data model lists it for that identity by
name (a common row alone does not count: the blank filing is the authority
on whether this form has the field), or it lies under a map the model types
as an object with no rows of its own (`scheduleNoItems`, created on
demand); every `MINIMAL_VALID` overlay, every manifest patch and every
manifest path (a numbered row read as the row path) is judged, with a
typo'd key, a stray row key, a map key, a numbered row and the Minors case
pinned synthetically. The overlay dropped the key; the Minors fill keeps
`wardName`, `ucn` and `ref`; both goldens regenerated (two variants gone, no
outcome changed, compared per type and label against HEAD; the notes say
so). *Evidence:* red first -- the rule against the tree as it was named
exactly `planMinor fixture: caseNumber`, the one finding across nine
fixtures and three manifests; green after, 19 of 19; `check:types` clean;
the goldens' specs 9 of 9; the fixture inventory, skip audit and 70T
guards 16 of 16. The closing regression then found the one consequence the
browser suite held: the year-rollover characterization's Minors record
still listed the key with the fixture's value, so `4f034486` regenerated
that record alone (the two caseNumber entries gone, nothing else changed,
the other eight records byte-identical; the note says why). The browser cases that write the Minors overlay were not run apart (port 4321 was held by the requester's own Playwright run throughout, and one browser run at a time is the rule); the closing full regression is their evidence, and nothing reads the key. *Cost:* unit-only, under an hour.

**Item 2 -- four skips relabelled.** *What a maintainer sees:* a run's skip
list no longer claims, four times, that the harness cannot exercise a
working feature. *The measured problem:* three skips in
`feature-load-failure.spec.ts` and one in `navigation-race.spec.ts` were
labelled `[environment-limitation]` (a browser or CI limit on a valid

### Delivery 7: Selective Historical Archiving

**Candidate files:** proposed `archive/testing/README.md` and
`archive/testing/suite-reference.json`, `file_index.md`; exact retired-tool paths
only after an audience/usefulness decision. No full in-repository snapshot.
**Checks:** verified commit/tag/path retrieval, catalogue links, optional external
snapshot checksum/access, absence of retired tools in active discovery.
**Estimated check time:** 1-5 minutes for reference/link/discovery checks; external
snapshot transfer/replay measured separately.
**Approval:** stable capture reference, tag creation if desired, external storage
and any tool move require explicit approval. No full/source/portable run needed
for a catalogue; ask before historical full replay.
**Exit:** a reader can find and retrieve historical tests/processes without
duplicating live fixtures or treating archived evidence as current coverage.

### Build record — BUILT 2026-10-15, `cc328fa6` (the requester's decisions that day: capture point `a5833f5`, no tag, no external snapshot)

*Two fixes the same evening, found by the push-to-master check of
Delivery 5 on the Delivery 7 push (run 38808218527, red at the catalogue's
own test):* the committed catalogue's short hashes were eight characters
and the runner derived seven -- git abbreviates just enough to be unique
in the repository it runs in, and this workstation's had grown to eight
with the day's objects. `793c9874` makes the generator take a fixed seven
from the full hash and adds a test that derives with git told to
abbreviate to eleven (red first with the old generator: all 25 entries
differed); `8dc3fae9` regenerates the catalogue and corrects which machine
had grown to eight. A third, `517bed23`, came from the closing regression's
first start: the C: copy has no `.git`, so the catalogue's three git-reading
tests failed there and `npm test` stopped before the browser suite; the
generator now finds the repository that holds its tree or takes
`PG_GIT_ROOT` from a copy (AGENTS.md section 1 says to set it), and the
spec pins both. The automatic runs on these pushes are the proof on the
runner, recorded in the closing section below.


**What a reader sees:** `archive/testing/README.md` -- where every retired
test and tool under `tests/` or `scripts/` last lived, the commit that
retired it and the `git show` that reads it back (25 files); the suite
before this remediation, as a commit with a GitHub tree link and a
download link for readers without Git and a worktree checkout for those
with it; the three comparisons against older builds that still run and
how; and every recorded baseline with its own note (36). Nothing is
copied, and the page says a green run of anything there says nothing
about today's suite. `suite-reference.json` beside it is the same in
machine-readable form.

**How it stays true:** `scripts/archive-catalogue.mjs --write` derives
both files from git history (`git log --diff-filter=D`), the comparisons it
lists and `tests/baseline/`, so a later deletion joins the retired list on
the next run and a recreated file leaves it; `tests/unit/archive-catalogue.spec.js`
fails when the files no longer say what the generator derives, when a
retired path still exists or its commit does not, when the capture point
or a path it names does not resolve, when a historical path or baseline is
missing, or when anything catalogued as retired is reachable from active
discovery (the index guard's roots).

**Checks, as the plan listed them:** verified commit and path retrieval
(the spec resolves the capture point and reads the latest retirement back
in full); catalogue links (the README's GitHub links carry the commit);
absence of retired tools in active discovery (the spec); optional external
snapshot -- none, by decision. Check time: the spec runs in about 3 s.

**Not done, and why:** no `retired-tools/` folder -- nothing retired is
both useful to the audience and inadequately reachable through the
catalogue and git, which is the plan's test for moving one; no tag and no
snapshot, by the requester's decision; no historical full replay (the plan
says ask first, and nobody asked for one).

## 10. Remediation Completion Standard

Deliveries 1, 1M and 2-4 are complete when execution pins the intended checkout/target/
browser, the backup regression cannot pass vacuously, executable governance
detects documented faults, historical-only jobs are separate, positive fixtures
and output helpers enforce their declared gate contracts, and minimal profile
membership plus target-case runtime/fault evidence prevents silent omissions.
A before/after full-source measurement on C: shows the cut in run time the
requester approved, with every removed case's failure still caught by a
retained one (Delivery 1M; added 2026-10-13 at the requester's decision).
The release sequence excludes quick/historical selectors, curated paths and
profile execution values each have one owner, and governance checks share
mechanics without merging their policies. Verified commands and sub-testing
instructions can then be adopted in AGENTS. No archive, mass reorganization,
new specialist suite or CI implementation is required to reach that boundary.

Retain independent artifact checks, real-control tests, readiness/sidebar/export
distinctions and meaningful ratchets. Keep red/fault evidence and exact reports
of counts/skips/retries/unexecuted coverage. Historical evidence is not release
proof; a green subset is not a release certificate. Optional deliveries remain
separately scoped; each delivery's build record above says what was built.
